lead_headline: Workflow SDK beta.6 lands schema bootstrapping as Cloudflare Workers blocker gets formally logged
lead_body: A dense Tuesday: workflow@5.0.0-beta.6 ships graphile-worker schema setup and a socket-path correction, while the node:vm conflict blocking Cloudflare Workers at least graduates from invisible to tracked. AI SDK led raw volume with Gemini 3.5 Flash, a streaming tool-call fix, and the Cerebras provider landing across both branches.
lead_article:
A genuinely busy Tuesday. The headline is Workflow SDK cutting workflow@5.0.0-beta.6, a release that arrived with graphile-worker schema bootstrapping in the setup CLI and a socket-file path fix that had been quietly causing grief. The Cloudflare Workers runtime is now formally blocked — a new issue tracks the node:vm dependency standing in the way — so that constraint is at least on the map rather than lurking. AI SDK shipped the most raw commit volume, with Gemini 3.5 Flash added to the Google provider, streaming tool-call argument serialization fixed, and the Cerebras chat provider landing on both main and the backport branch. Stream-resuming work is still in progress — the branch shows the usual pattern of failing snapshots and iterative fixes that precede a merge.

Astro's main movement was exposing route asset URLs on middleware context, with both a v6 PR and a v5 backport opened in the same afternoon. Two HMR fixes also landed — one invalidating importer modules in the runner cache, another invalidating the route cache when module identity shifts — which together address the class of stale-cache bugs that have been surfacing on static-path routes. Hydrogen added generic cart type support and opened a PR for cart fragment override typing, a quiet but coherent feature arc. Claude Code shipped two patch releases, v2.1.144 and v2.1.145, against a backdrop of eleven issues opened today — worktree regressions, background-session failures, the LFS proxy rejection on the web client, and the context-spec regression from 2.1.144 that deserves attention first. Gemma.cpp saw two PRs: LM-only model variants for Gemma 3 and a flash-attention link-error fix on multi-target SIMD builds. Metaflow's single PR prevents duplicate DAG task names in foreach-plus-split-switch flows — a correctness fix, not glamorous, but the kind that surfaces only once someone has been burned by it.
